assets.title: Assets
assets.subtitle: A balance-sheet stocktake: net worth = assets − liabilities. Record a balance on a date, not every transaction.
assets.emptyBody: Record what you own and what you owe separately. Money in a bank account is an asset; an unpaid card balance is a liability. A home and a car count in net worth, and they are not cash you can spend.
assets.starterHint: One line is enough to begin.

summary.liquidHint: Cash, investments, and receivables, minus high-interest debt, installments, and other payables

focus.start: One cash balance or one bank account is enough to start. Record debts you have, and leave the column empty if you have none.
focus.high_interest: There is high-interest short-term debt. It is not the same as a mortgage: nothing backs it, and it keeps taking from what you have left. Read that unpaid balance on its own.
focus.emergency: Cash does not yet cover 3 months of essential spending. Set that cash aside before placing the rest anywhere else.
focus.set_essential: Add one month of essential spending so the emergency fund can be read as a number of months. Essentials are the costs you cannot pause.
focus.excess_cash: Cash covers more than 12 months of essential spending. The amount above that range does not all need to sit in a checking account.
focus.balanced: Net worth, spendable money, and the emergency fund are separate figures. Next time, update the balances.

columns.liabilitiesEmpty: No liabilities. Leave this empty if you owe nothing.

profile.title: This book
profile.currencyHint: The whole book uses one currency. Convert a foreign balance at a price you accept, then record it.
profile.currencyLocked: The currency stays fixed once a line exists. Remove every line before changing it.
profile.essentialHint: Costs you cannot pause: housing, food, transport, insurance. Leave out spending you can stop.

principles.title: How to read this
principles.item1: Net worth is assets minus liabilities. Record what you own and what you owe separately. Do not net a card balance against a bank balance first.
principles.item2: A home and a car count in net worth, and they are not money you can spend. Spendable net worth is cash, investments, and receivables, minus high-interest debt, installments, and other payables.
principles.item3: The emergency fund is how many months of essential spending your cash covers. Essentials are costs you cannot pause. A common range is 3 to 6 months.
principles.item4: Keep high-interest short-term debt apart from the mortgage. The mortgage is backed by the home. A card balance is not.
principles.item5: This is a balance stocktake, not a transaction ledger. Recheck cash about monthly, investments quarterly, and a home or vehicle yearly at a price you could sell for. Balances older than 35 days are marked for review.

categoryHints.cash: Checking, money-market cash, and cash on hand. Counts toward the emergency fund.
categoryHints.investment: Funds, shares, bonds. Counts as spendable net worth, not as emergency cash.
categoryHints.property: A home or other property, at a price you accept, not the original purchase price.
categoryHints.durable: A car or valuables, at a rough sale price, not the original price.
categoryHints.other_asset: Use this only when nothing else fits.
categoryHints.credit: Unpaid card or consumer-loan principal. Do not mix it with a mortgage.
categoryHints.installment: Remaining principal on a car loan or other installment.
categoryHints.mortgage: Remaining mortgage principal. Include it with the property, or exclude both.
categoryHints.payable: Money you owe people, or a payment that is already fixed.
categoryHints.other_liability: Use this only when nothing else fits.
